titre: FCC authorization before marketing digital devices
citation: unintentional radiators shall be authorized prior to the initiation of marketing, pursuant to the procedures for certification or Supplier's Declaration of Conformity (SDoC) given in subpart J of part 2 of this chapter

note: Table 1 of the same paragraph lists 'Class B personal computers and peripherals' and 'Class B external switching power supplies' with 'SDoC or Certification'. § 15.19(a)(3) of the same part requires a compliance statement on the device and § 2.1077(a)(3) says the responsible party for an SDoC must be located within the United States, which matters for a brand established abroad. FCC appears in the laptop marks, not in the charger marks.

titre: FCC certification of the radio transmitter

titre: DOE efficiency standard for external power supplies
citation: all direct operation external power supplies manufactured on or after February 10, 2016, shall meet the following standards
exigence: A direct operation external power supply manufactured on or after February 10, 2016 must meet the DOE energy conservation standards set out in the table of that paragraph.
note: The sentence begins 'Except as provided in paragraphs (w)(5), (w)(6), and (w)(7)'. The numeric limits sit in a table that the official renderer serves as an image, so the values and power ranges were not read here. § 430.2 defines a direct operation external power supply as one that can operate a consumer product that is not a battery charger without the assistance of a battery. The classification of this USB PD charger (direct operation, adaptive) must be confirmed by the manufacturer. The date is a date of manufacture. § 429.12(a) also requires the manufacturer to submit a certification report to DOE before distributing a basic model in commerce.

titre: California appliance efficiency certification by manufacturer
citation: A new appliance manufactured on or after the effective date of the standards or other cost-effective measures shall not be sold or offered for sale in the state, unless it is certified by the manufacturer of the appliance to be in compliance with the standards or other cost-effective measures.
exigence: A new appliance covered by a California efficiency standard may be sold or offered for sale in California only if its manufacturer has certified that it complies with that standard.
note: State of California only. The same paragraph says 'sold or offered for sale in the state' covers internet and mail order sales for end use in the state, regardless of the seller's physical location. This statute does not itself name computers: the product scope sits in California Code of Regulations, Title 20, sections 1601 to 1609, whose official site refused the download (see gaps). A CEC compliance advisory of April 8, 2021 read on energy.ca.gov states that those sections contain standards, certification requirements and marking requirements for computers. acte: Executive Order 14388 of February 20, 2026, revising section 2 of Executive Order 14324 of July 30, 2025
autorite: President of the United States; enforced by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
article: Sec. 2, revised section 2(a) of Executive Order 14324
citation: Accordingly, all such shipments, except those sent through the international postal network, shall be subject to all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges.
exigence: A low-value shipment that is not sent through the international postal network no longer enters duty free and bears all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions and charges.

autorite: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), U.S. Department of Transportation

titre: Compliance with Canadian radio technical standards
autorite: Parliament of Canada; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
citation: No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, lease, offer for sale or sell any radio apparatus, interference-causing equipment or radio-sensitive equipment for which technical standards have been established under paragraph 6(1)(a), unless the apparatus or equipment complies with those standards.
exigence: Nobody may import, offer for sale or sell in Canada radio apparatus or interference-causing equipment covered by ISED technical standards unless it complies with those standards.
note: Subsection 4(2) adds that equipment for which a technical acceptance certificate is required may only be imported or sold in accordance with that certificate. For the charger, ICES-003 issue 7 section 1.2.3 says an external switched mode power supply marketed separately is under the scope of ICES-001 and may instead be authorized under ICES-003 if intended exclusively for devices within its scope. titre: Energy efficiency standard for imported power supplies
acte: Energy Efficiency Act (S.C. 1992, c. 36), with Energy Efficiency Regulations, 2016 (SOR/2016-311), sections 586 to 589
autorite: Parliament of Canada; Natural Resources Canada
citation: No dealer shall, for the purpose of sale or lease, ship an energy-using product from one province to another province, or import an energy-using product into Canada, unless
exigence: A dealer may import an energy-using product into Canada for sale only if the product complies with the energy efficiency standard and is labelled as the regulations require.
note: The conditions that follow 'unless' are (a) the product complies with the energy efficiency standard and (b) the product or its package is labelled in accordance with the regulations, if any. Section 587(1) of the Regulations prescribes an external power supply as an energy-using product, and for units made on or after July 1, 2017 the exclusion of adaptive external power supplies no longer applies. Section 588 sets the standards (direct operation: CSA C381.1-17, Table D.1). Section 4(4) of the Regulations waives the verification mark when the unit carries the US DOE International Efficiency Marking Protocol mark, a certification body has verified the energy performance information, and the model number matches. 'Dealer' means a person engaged in the business of importing, manufacturing or selling such products: whether a foreign online seller shipping to a consumer is the dealer was not settled here. Section 5 of the Act requires dealers to report prescribed information to the Minister.

titre: NOM-019 safety of data processing equipment
acte: NOM-019-SCFI-1998, Seguridad de equipo de procesamiento de datos
autorite: Secretaría de Economía (formerly Secretaría de Comercio y Fomento Industrial)
citation: Esta Norma Oficial Mexicana establece los requisitos de seguridad que deben cumplir todos los equipos de procesamiento de datos periféricos o equipos relacionados, que se comercialicen en el territorio de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos.

titre: NOM-029 efficiency certificate for power supplies
acte: NOM-029-ENER-2017, Eficiencia energética de fuentes de alimentación externa. Límites, métodos de prueba, marcado y etiquetado
autorite: Secretaría de Energía, Comisión Nacional para el Uso Eficiente de la Energía (CONUEE)
citation: Todo producto comprendido en el campo de aplicación de esta NOM que se importe, fabrique, comercialice, así como los que se distribuyan o suministren con fines promocionales dentro del territorio nacional, debe contar con certificado de conformidad de producto de acuerdo con esta NOM.
exigence: An external power supply within the scope of this standard that is imported or marketed in Mexico must hold a product certificate of conformity under the standard.
note: Scope: external power supplies that convert AC line voltage to a single fixed DC output voltage at a time, with maximum output power of 250,0 W or less, sold individually or with an end product. A definition covers units with built-in mechanisms that select an output voltage from a preset menu, tested at the lowest and highest levels, but the fit of a USB PD charger should be confirmed with a certification body. Section 10.1 requires marking the efficiency level V or VI in Roman numerals. The text enters into force 180 calendar days after its publication. Certificates are granted to persons established in Mexico or from countries with a free trade agreement.

titre: Homologation of radio equipment in Mexico
acte: Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión
autorite: Congreso de la Unión; Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones (the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones continues during the transition)
citation: Los productos, equipos, dispositivos o aparatos destinados a telecomunicaciones o radiodifusión que puedan ser conectados a una red de telecomunicaciones o hacer uso del espectro radioeléctrico deberán homologarse conforme a las normas o disposiciones técnicas aplicables
exigence: A product that can connect to a telecommunications network or use the radio spectrum, such as a laptop with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, must be homologated under the applicable technical standards.
note: The same article says the applicant for homologation must have an address in Mexico, which matters for a brand established abroad. The decree says it enters into force the day after its publication in the Diario Oficial and that the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones continues in office until the plenary of the new Commission is formed. The homologation guidelines published by the IFT (DOF note 5639645) were opened but not quoted. No Mexican homologation number is in the laptop marks list.
